title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From the lucky number 13 to the symbolic torchlight descent, Colgate University's traditions are deeply rooted in its 1817 founding and the unique geography of 'The Hill.'

cards.title: The Lucky Number 13
cards.subtitle: A founding legacy of 13 men, dollars, and prayers
cards.notes: Embrace the number 13, which appears in the zip code, campus speed limits, and the university address. It honors the 13 founders who started the school with $13 and 13 prayers.
cards.short_summary: Colgate's most pervasive tradition celebrates the number 13 as a symbol of good fortune rather than a superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: Colgate University was founded by 13 men with 13 dollars and 13 prayers; the number is now integrated into the campus speed limit (13 mph) and address (13 Oak Drive).
cards.access_notes: Visible campus-wide through signage and official university branding.

cards.title: Senior Torchlight Procession
cards.subtitle: The symbolic descent from the Hill
cards.notes: Join the graduating class on the eve of Commencement as they carry torches down the hill and through Willow Path, symbolizing the light of knowledge entering the world.
cards.short_summary: A century-old graduation rite where seniors process down the hill with lit torches to signify their transition to alumni status.
cards.evidence_claim: The Senior Torchlight Procession began in 1930 and involves graduates processing from the Academic Quad down to Taylor Lake on the night before graduation.
cards.access_notes: Held annually during Commencement Weekend; spectators are welcome at designated viewing areas.

cards.title: Colgate Day
cards.subtitle: Celebrating every Friday the 13th
cards.notes: Wear your best maroon gear whenever Friday falls on the 13th. This worldwide celebration connects students and alumni through social media and local campus events.
cards.short_summary: A recurring holiday celebrated by the Colgate community every time a Friday the 13th occurs on the calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Colgate Day is an official university tradition celebrated every Friday the 13th, where the community wears maroon and participates in spirit events.
cards.access_notes: Occurs on every Friday the 13th; events are held on campus and in alumni chapters globally.

cards.title: The Willow Path Legend
cards.subtitle: A walk toward destiny
cards.notes: Walk the scenic path along Taylor Lake. Legend says that couples who have their first kiss on the Willow Path bridge are destined to marry.
cards.short_summary: A romantic campus superstition centered on the historic willow-lined walkway and its small bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Willow Path legend suggests that a first kiss on the path's bridge leads to marriage; the path itself was restored with 25 new willows in 1989.
cards.source_title: Beloved landmarks: Taylor Lake and the Willow Path | Colgate at 200 Years
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily; the path runs along the north shore of Taylor Lake.

cards.title: Konosioni Torch Medals
cards.subtitle: Gratitude for the Colgate community
cards.notes: Seniors present these medals to faculty or staff who made a meaningful impact on their college journey, a tradition led by the Konosioni Senior Honor Society.
cards.short_summary: A senior-year tradition of expressing gratitude to mentors through the presentation of symbolic medals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Torch Medal tradition was inspired by the Konosioni Senior Honor Society to recognize the impact of faculty and staff on the student experience.
cards.access_notes: Medals are distributed to seniors during their final year for presentation to chosen mentors.

cards.title: The Colgate Hello
cards.subtitle: A century of campus friendliness
cards.notes: Keep the tradition alive by greeting fellow community members as you pass them on the Hill. This practice dates back to at least the 1920s.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing social custom encouraging students and faculty to greet one another while walking on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Colgate Hello' was first mentioned in the 1924-25 Student Handbook and remains a promoted cultural practice on campus today.
cards.access_notes: An informal social tradition practiced daily across the entire campus.

cards.title: Founders' Day Convocation
cards.subtitle: Welcoming the first-year class
cards.notes: Attend this formal ceremony during orientation to mark your official entry into the academic community, featuring a procession and a keynote address.
cards.short_summary: The capstone orientation event that formally initiates new students into the university's history and values.
cards.evidence_claim: Founders' Day Convocation is the formal welcoming event for the first-year class, held at the end of orientation before fall classes begin.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late August; primarily for first-year students and faculty.

cards.title: Room Return
cards.subtitle: Seniors revisiting their first-year roots
cards.notes: During Springfest, seniors visit their former first-year dorm rooms to meet current residents and share memories of their early days on the Hill.
cards.short_summary: A nostalgic tradition where graduating seniors return to their original residence halls to connect with underclassmen.
cards.evidence_claim: Room Return is a senior tradition held during Springfest where seniors revisit their first and second-year dorms to reminisce and meet current occupants.
cards.source_title: Springfest Weekend 2026 Boasts Jam-Packed Itinerary, New Traditions
cards.access_notes: Takes place in residence halls across campus during Springfest weekend.

cards.title: Old Colgate Spirit
cards.subtitle: The song of the thirteen men
cards.notes: Learn the lyrics to this iconic campus song that recounts the story of the 13 founders. It is often performed by the Colgate Thirteen a cappella group.
cards.short_summary: A traditional university song that immortalizes the story of the school's founding in 1819.
cards.evidence_claim: The song 'Old Colgate Spirit' includes lyrics about the 13 prayers and 13 dollars that founded the university and is a staple of campus events.
cards.access_notes: Performed at athletic events, convocations, and by student musical groups.

cards.title: The Numbered Boulders of Peter's Glen
cards.subtitle: A countdown in stone
cards.notes: Explore the staircase in Peter's Glen to find boulders engraved with numbers counting down from 13, a subtle nod to the university's favorite number.
cards.short_summary: A series of engraved boulders along a campus nature path that integrate the number 13 into the landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Peter's Glen features a staircase with boulders engraved with descending numbers starting from 13 at the top.
cards.source_title: The Number 13: How We Can Count on Colgate
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the walking path near the ALANA Cultural Center.
